projects.title: DeepPrep-AI
projects.summary: DeepPrep-AI: A Multimodal Interview Analysis Tool for Personalized Feedback
stack: ML / Modeling: PyTorch, TensorFlow, MediaPipe, OpenCV, Librosa, EfficientNet-B0 pretrained on ImageNet using AdamW with dropout and weight decay

overview.problem: Interviews are high-stakes, yet most candidates receive little to no actionable feedback on their performance. When feedback is given, it is often subjective, inconsistent, or delayed, making it difficult to identify specific areas for improvement.
overview.built: A system that can objectively evaluate interview behavior and generate meaningful, actionable feedback at scale.

results: DeepPrep-AI demonstrates a practical multimodal approach to interview analysis by combining posture, engagement, and audio signals into a unified feedback system. The project is motivated by a real gap in interview preparation: the lack of specific, consistent, and actionable feedback. Using RecruitView as the benchmark dataset, the system frames interview assessment as a continuous multimodal regression problem and uses specialized neural networks for each behavioral component. The current implementation already displays accurate engagement results with feedback generation and shows promising subsystem level improvements through targeted fine tuning.

projects.title: Misinformation Detection
projects.summary: Misinformation Detection System to classify content as accurate or inaccurate
stack: Baseline: TF-IDF (unigrams + bigrams) with logistic regression
Transformer models: DeBERTa-v3 hybrid fine-tuned for sequence classification
Training: Class-weighted cross-entropy for label imbalance, different learning rates for the encoder and the classification head, gradient clipping, dropout, data augmentation

overview.problem: Misinformation circulating on digital platforms has become a serious threat to public discourse, institutional trust, and informed decision making.
overview.built: A system to detect misinformation in various forms of content using benchmark datasets that combine textual, contextual, and metadata features with a transformer based language model, DistilBERT.

results: Developed a data ingestion pipeline that loads the LIAR dataset (train/valid/test split) into a pandas dataframe. A baseline classifier was implemented using TF-IDF vectorization (unigrams and bigrams) with logistic regression on the statement text only. Went through multiple different model and landed on the hybrid DeBERTa v3 model achieved a highest 92.8% training accuracy, 75.6% validation accuracy, and 72.7% test accuracy.

projects.title: Lava Lamp Password (LLP)
projects.summary: Lava Lamp Password (LLP) utilizes the randomness of lava lamps to create a completely random and secure password that is displayed on a screen.
stack: Hardware: Pynq (FPGA) board, 1080p camera, LCD Display

overview.problem: Passwords in use are prone to being predictable. A GOOD password needs to be random and unrelated to anything personal/predictable.
overview.built: LLP utilizes the randomness of lava lamps, a technique used by large industries such as Cloudflare, to periodically pass captured images through a key derivation algorithm that produces a secure 15-character key. Each frame is decoded into its RGB values, successive frames are differenced to produce transition frames, and those transition frames are differenced again, isolating the unpredictable motion of the lamps from the static background. Singular value decomposition is then applied to decorrelate the data and remove structural regularity, and reservoir sampling reduces it to a fixed-size sample, adding a second source of uncertainty. The sampled values are mapped to a 15-character key drawn from a–z, A–Z, 0–9 and !@#$%^&()+.

results: A completely random 15-character key drawn from a–z, A–Z, 0–9 and !@#$%^&()+.
